lessons.name: NCCR Automation
lessons.summary: NCCR Automation is a Swiss research network developing methods for reliable, responsible automation across interconnected real-world systems.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

NCCR Automation is a Swiss research network developing methods for reliable, responsible automation across interconnected real-world systems.

![NCCR Automation group gathered outdoors](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-nccr.webp)
*Group photograph published by NCCR Automation. Source: [Official source](https://nccr-automation.ch/about), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Automation** means making a system act without a person choosing every action; the network studies its mathematical and engineering foundations.
- **Control** chooses actions from measurements; NCCR connects learning, optimization, and control with responsibility and sustainability.
- **Connected applications** include energy and mobility, so a robot is one possible participant rather than the network’s only subject.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Shared doorway] --> B[Compare access rules]
 B --> C[Count deliveries and waits]
```

> **Key idea:** Improving one controller is not enough when its decisions affect other people and interconnected systems.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think distributed systems:** independently reasonable controllers can conflict, just as services can overload a shared database.
- **A worked thought experiment:** two simulated delivery robots share one doorway; compare “always go” against a rule that grants access to one robot.
- **Measure the trade-off:** count completed deliveries and waiting time separately; a fast robot that permanently blocks its neighbor is not a good shared solution.

## How to engage

1. **Browse the research challenges** to distinguish enabling algorithms from questions about their consequences.
2. **Watch the fairness demonstration** before tackling its mathematical details; identify the shared resource and the competing objectives.
3. **Follow the public seminar series** and prepare one precise question tied to your small simulation, rather than requesting an undefined collaboration.

lessons.name: ONERA – DTIS
lessons.summary: ONERA’s DTIS department develops information-processing and systems methods for aerospace, including perception, autonomous decisions, and robotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ONERA’s DTIS department develops information-processing and systems methods for aerospace, including perception, autonomous decisions, and robotics.

![Mana and Effibot ground robots during the Action demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-onera.webp)
*A planned rendezvous between Mana and Effibot during the historical Action demonstration. © ONERA. Source: [Official source](https://www.onera.fr/fr/actualites/une-equipe-de-douze-drones-et-robots-en-mission-autonome), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Perception** turns sensor measurements into useful information about the surroundings; DTIS studies it alongside information processing and system design.
- **Autonomy** combines understanding a situation with deciding and executing actions; its scientific themes include robotics and artificial intelligence.
- **Experimental platforms** connect algorithms to real vehicles and sensors rather than stopping at an isolated machine-learning score.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Sensor measurements] --> B[Perception]
 B --> C[Decide together]
 C --> D[Vehicle actions]
```

> **Key idea:** Aerospace autonomy is a complete system problem, not simply a detector attached to a moving machine.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Use a services analogy:** perception, planning, and execution expose different interfaces, but the whole mission fails when their assumptions disagree.
- **Historical worked example:** the 2015 Action demonstration coordinated twelve vehicles, including four simulated vehicles; this was not twelve physical robots.
- **Student-scale exercise:** replay one recorded scene, label obstacles, and compare a route before and after one obstacle is added; no aircraft is needed.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Action demonstration** as a historical case study, not a claim about today’s deployable fleet.
2. **Read DTIS’s scientific themes** and choose one software-sized question, such as representing uncertainty in an obstacle map.
3. **Use the public department pages** to find relevant teams and published work; share a reproducible simulation and a focused technical question.

lessons.name: OST Institute for Lab Automation and Mechatronics (ILT)
lessons.summary: OST’s Institute for Lab Automation and Mechatronics develops applied robotic systems that connect sensing, manipulation, mobility, and industrial workflows.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OST’s Institute for Lab Automation and Mechatronics develops applied robotic systems that connect sensing, manipulation, mobility, and industrial workflows.

![Robot arms and mobile platforms in the OST ILT robotics laboratory](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-ilt.webp)
*Robotics equipment pictured on ILT’s robotics competence page. Source: [Official source](https://www.ost.ch/en/research-and-consulting-services/technology/mechanical-engineering/ilt-institute-for-lab-automation-and-mechatronics/competences/robotics), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mechatronics** combines mechanical parts, electronics, and software into one working machine; ILT applies this integration to laboratory and industrial automation.
- **Mobile manipulation** puts a robot arm on a moving base; ILT’s smart mobile manipulator combines these parts with an expandable software framework.
- **Pick and place** means finding, grasping, moving, and releasing an object; ILT publishes a collaborative-robot example alongside its broader robotics work.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Navigate] --> B[Align]
 B --> C[Grasp]
 C --> D[Check result]
```

> **Key idea:** Useful automation must fit the entire workplace task, including travel, object handling, and interfaces to existing equipment.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think integration testing:** a correct grasp function is insufficient if the robot arrives at the wrong station or receives the wrong object location.
- **Worked decomposition:** split “fetch a sample” into three software states: navigate, align, and grasp; record which state fails instead of one vague failure flag.
- **Start smaller than their hardware:** replay a camera recording and implement the state transitions before considering a moving platform or physical arm.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the institute’s robotics overview** and identify the sensors, robot arms, and mobile bases rather than treating everything as “AI.”
2. **Read a concrete project page** to list its inputs, outputs, and integration constraints.
3. **Use ILT’s public project contacts** for a focused technical exchange supported by a short demo and clear experimental results.

lessons.name: PEPR O2R (Organic Robotics programme)
lessons.summary: PEPR O2R is a French research programme developing robotics that adapts to people, environments, and social needs rather than imposing one fixed design.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

PEPR O2R is a French research programme developing robotics that adapts to people, environments, and social needs rather than imposing one fixed design.

![Prosthetic robotic hand and experimental equipment in the REINVENT project photograph](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-o2r.webp)
*Prosthesis research illustrated by the O2R REINVENT project. © Philippe Gauthier – ISIR. Source: [Official source](https://www.pepr-o2r.fr/projet/reinvent/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Organic robotics** is the programme’s approach to adaptable robots considered together with their environment and social context; it does not simply mean biological materials.
- **REINVENT** investigates prostheses, artificial devices that replace missing body parts, with attention to their users and everyday experience.
- **ASSISTMOV** studies movement assistance, linking robotic technologies with human needs rather than optimizing a mechanism in isolation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[User needs] --> B[Prototype assistance]
 B --> C[Test with users]
 C --> A
```

> **Key idea:** A technically successful robot can still be the wrong solution if it ignores the person who must live with it.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think user-centered APIs:** a clean internal implementation is not enough when the interface makes the user’s actual task harder.
- **Worked design exercise:** compare two proposed assistance interfaces, a continuous joystick and three discrete buttons; list which user actions each requires before choosing algorithms.
- **Keep the scope honest:** a student interface prototype can explore usability questions; it is not evidence of a safe or effective medical device.

## How to engage

1. **Read the programme introduction** to understand why robotics, human sciences, and design appear together.
2. **Explore one targeted project** and write down its user, environment, and research question.
3. **Watch a public O2R webinar** and follow announced scientific events; bring a specific question rather than assuming programme participation is open automatically.

lessons.name: Pprime
lessons.summary: Pprime is a French physics and engineering institute whose robotics work includes dexterous manipulation, collaborative robots, and biomechanics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Pprime is a French physics and engineering institute whose robotics work includes dexterous manipulation, collaborative robots, and biomechanics.

![Research facility pictured by Institut Pprime](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-pprime.webp)
*An experimental facility pictured on Pprime’s institute presentation. Source: [Official source](https://www.pprime.fr/institut/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Dexterous manipulation** means controlling how an object is held or moved, not merely closing a gripper around it.
- **DextRobUP** is Pprime’s platform for dexterous, industrial, open, and collaborative robotics, including assistance to people in production environments.
- **Biomechanics** studies the mechanics of living movement; it provides another connection between Pprime’s engineering research and human-centered robot design.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Object and task] --> B[Choose grasp]
 B --> C[Move fingers]
 C --> D[Check grip and damage]
```

> **Key idea:** Manipulation research studies the coupled behavior of the object, robot mechanism, sensors, and person—not just the arm trajectory.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think interface contracts:** a command such as “grasp” hides assumptions about object shape, contact, and what the fingers can physically do.
- **Worked exercise:** compare lifting a rigid block and a paper cup; list how the same finger-closing command could succeed once and crush the other object.
- **Separate outcomes:** record “held securely” and “object undamaged” as different checks; this makes a manipulation demo more meaningful than a motion-only video.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the university-linked laboratory visit** for a visual introduction to dexterous-robot equipment; the video’s playful title is not a hardware purchasing recommendation.
2. **Read DextRobUP’s platform description** to connect visible machines with actual research questions.
3. **Consult Pprime’s public partnership information** before proposing a narrowly scoped experiment; access to research equipment is not implied by its online description.

lessons.name: Rhoban (LaBRI, Bordeaux)
lessons.summary: Rhoban is a Bordeaux robotics team developing autonomous humanoids, with public hardware and software that make robot behavior inspectable.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Rhoban is a Bordeaux robotics team developing autonomous humanoids, with public hardware and software that make robot behavior inspectable.

![Rhoban SigmaBan humanoid robots on a RoboCup football field](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-rhoban.webp)
*SigmaBan humanoids on a RoboCup football field, as pictured by Rhoban. Source: [Official source](https://www.rhoban.com/post/sigmaban), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **SigmaBan** is Rhoban’s humanoid football platform; a humanoid has a body arrangement inspired by people, including legs for walking.
- **Microban** is an open-source, fully 3D-printable small humanoid; its repository brings a physical robot closer to something students can inspect and reproduce.
- **Placo** provides planning and control software: deciding desired movement and computing how the robot should achieve it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[See ball] --> B[Choose movement]
 B --> C[Command joints]
 C --> A
```

> **Key idea:** Robot football exposes the whole autonomy stack because seeing the ball is useless unless the robot can move and stay upright.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a running application:** vision, motion decisions, and joint commands must work together, not merely pass separate notebook tests.
- **Worked exercise:** label ten frames with the ball left or right; implement a two-action “turn left / turn right” decision before attempting a walking controller.
- **Open does not mean effortless:** read hardware and software requirements separately; printable body parts do not replace actuators, electronics, or calibration.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Microban’s walking demonstration** and distinguish the small platform from the larger SigmaBan pictured above.
2. **Read the Microban repository** and its assembly information before deciding whether a hardware build fits your team.
3. **Study Placo’s examples** and report a minimal reproducible software issue, or improve documentation after reproducing an existing example.

lessons.name: Robotics Institute Germany (RIG)
lessons.summary: Robotics Institute Germany connects German robotics research organizations through shared research, infrastructure, education, and transfer activities.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Institute Germany connects German robotics research organizations through shared research, infrastructure, education, and transfer activities.

![Robotics infrastructure at the TUM AI Factory, pictured by RIG](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-rig.webp)
*The TUM AI Factory infrastructure photo published by RIG; photograph Andreas Heddergott / TUM. Source: [Official source](https://robotics-institute-germany.de/about-us/), Free for use in reporting on TUM, with the copyright noted.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A network, not one robot:** RIG brings research institutions together rather than presenting a single machine or manufacturer’s product range.
- **Shared infrastructure** means facilities and resources that support experiments across research groups; RIG connects this with methods, benchmarks, and transfer.
- **Education and training** include public learning activities, while its lecture series exposes research topics such as touch-based robot perception.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Research groups] --> B[Shared tools and tests]
 B --> C[Compare results]
 C --> D[Exchange knowledge]
```

> **Key idea:** Shared experiments and learning infrastructure can make robotics knowledge travel farther than a single impressive laboratory demonstration.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a software foundation:** common tools and evaluation practices help independent teams compare results instead of maintaining incompatible private stacks.
- **Worked study exercise:** choose two grasping demos and compare their objects, sensors, and success definitions; different test conditions can explain different-looking results.
- **Use the network as a directory:** identify the group behind a particular method rather than assuming every German robotics result is produced centrally by RIG.

## How to engage

1. **Start with RIG’s introduction** to understand its scope and the distinction between member institutions and network activities.
2. **Browse its education offerings** and check individual event conditions before making participation plans.
3. **Watch a public lecture** with your team; summarize one experimental assumption and one question you can test in a small student project.

lessons.name: Shanghai AI Laboratory
lessons.summary: Shanghai AI Laboratory develops embodied-AI research tools including InternVLA-M1 for robot actions and InternUtopia for simulated environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Shanghai AI Laboratory develops embodied-AI research tools including InternVLA-M1 for robot actions and InternUtopia for simulated environments.

![Physical robot arm above a table of objects in the InternVLA-M1 demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-shanghai.webp)
*Frame from the project’s published real-robot pick-and-place video. Source: [Official source](https://internrobotics.github.io/internvla-m1.github.io/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Embodied AI** connects an AI system’s decisions to actions inside an environment, instead of producing only text or image labels.
- **InternVLA-M1** is a vision-language-action framework: it combines visual information and language instructions to guide robotic manipulation, meaning the handling of objects.
- **InternUtopia (ex-GRUtopia)** provides a simulation platform for embodied-AI research; simulation is a software environment for testing agents without each trial requiring hardware.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Image and instruction] --> B[Locate target]
 B --> C[Predict actions]
 C --> D[Robot movement]
```

> **Key idea:** Understanding the words in an instruction and locating its target are different problems from reliably executing the required motion.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a compiler pipeline:** an instruction must be grounded in the scene before it can become useful low-level actions.
- **Worked example:** for “put the grapes in the basket,” identify the grapes and basket first; correct language interpretation alone does not prove a successful placement.
- **Keep evaluation separate:** inspect which tasks use simulated scenes and which show physical robots; do not treat the two as interchangeable evidence.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the project demonstration** and track one command from scene understanding to observable object movement.
2. **Read the project overview** before choosing between the action-model and simulator repositories; they solve different parts of the problem.
3. **Inspect repository setup and licenses** before downloading assets; contribute a reproducible issue or a documented small experiment rather than claiming general robot intelligence.

lessons.name: Stanford Robotics Center
lessons.summary: Stanford Robotics Center brings researchers and shared facilities together to develop robots for domestic, medical, industrial, and other real-world settings.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Stanford Robotics Center brings researchers and shared facilities together to develop robots for domestic, medical, industrial, and other real-world settings.

![Interior of the Stanford Robotics Center research facility](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-stanford.webp)
*Inside the Stanford Robotics Center’s shared research facility. Source: [Official source](https://src.stanford.edu), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Interdisciplinary robotics** combines different specialties; the center describes research spanning household tasks, healthcare, manufacturing, field work, and human interaction.
- **Domestic robotics** studies robots operating around everyday human objects and environments, rather than only tightly arranged factory workstations.
- **SOAR**, Stanford Older Adult Robotics, is a flagship initiative developing robots to support older adults and caregivers in everyday activities.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Everyday needs] --> B[Research projects]
 B --> C[Shared facilities]
 C --> D[Evaluate applications]
```

> **Key idea:** A research center provides a shared place and infrastructure for many robotics questions, not one universal robot architecture.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a shared test environment:** common space and equipment make it easier to compare experiments across teams than unrelated one-off setups.
- **Worked exercise:** evaluate one household pick-up task with three object positions; keep the camera and success rule fixed so comparisons mean something.
- **Look beyond the highlight:** the center’s OceanOne video illustrates underwater manipulation; it is a different research setting from its domestic-robot learning projects.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a concrete robot demonstration** to see how the environment constrains sensing and movement.
2. **Browse the domestic-robotics and SOAR pages** to see assistive applications; choose a software-scale question without presenting a student demo as validated care technology.
3. **Follow the center’s public projects and events**; use project-specific resources and published contacts rather than assuming facility access or collaboration is automatic.

lessons.name: Swiss Drone and Robotics Centre (SDRC)
lessons.summary: The Swiss Drone and Robotics Centre evaluates unmanned systems and helps connect robotics research with Swiss security and disaster-relief needs.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The Swiss Drone and Robotics Centre evaluates unmanned systems and helps connect robotics research with Swiss security and disaster-relief needs.

![ANYmal rescue robot pictured by the Swiss Drone and Robotics Centre](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-sdrc.webp)
*The SDRC publishes this rescue-robot ANYmal photograph, credited to DDPS. Source: [Official source](https://www.ar.admin.ch/en/sdrc-en), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Unmanned systems** operate without a person onboard; the term includes drones and ground robots and does not automatically imply fully autonomous behavior.
- **ARCHE** assesses advanced robotic capabilities for hazardous environments, with disaster relief providing concrete scenarios rather than only laboratory benchmarks.
- **Technology transfer** connects research prototypes with prospective operational users; SDRC also describes testing infrastructure and collaboration with research and industry partners.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Research prototype] --> B[Realistic field test]
 B --> C[User feedback]
 C --> D[Improve robustness]
```

> **Key idea:** Field testing asks whether a capability survives a useful scenario, not merely whether the robot can perform it once indoors.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think staging versus production:** a rescue-site obstacle, unreliable connection, or unexpected surface can expose assumptions hidden by a clean development environment.
- **Worked exercise:** replay a recorded inspection route twice, hiding every fifth camera frame on the second run; compare how your perception code handles missing observations.
- **Stay within student scope:** software replay and simulation can teach robustness without entering a hazardous site or operating a vehicle near emergency personnel.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official ARCHE recap** to identify the kinds of machines and tasks being assessed.
2. **Read the ARCHE description** before interpreting a demonstration as an operationally approved rescue capability.
3. **Follow the centre’s public information and contacts** for relevant research activities; do not assume that a public event report grants access to its test facilities.

lessons.name: TIMC
lessons.summary: TIMC is a Grenoble-area health-engineering laboratory whose medical-robotics research connects imaging, modelling, and assistance to clinical procedures.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TIMC is a Grenoble-area health-engineering laboratory whose medical-robotics research connects imaging, modelling, and assistance to clinical procedures.

![TIMC laboratory terrace and building pictured on the laboratory website](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-timc.webp)
*The TIMC laboratory’s building and terrace, pictured on its official website. Source: [Official source](https://www.timc.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **GMCAO**, TIMC’s computer-assisted medical and surgical intervention team, develops methods and devices that help clinicians perform precise procedures.
- **Medical imaging** supplies information about anatomy; data fusion combines measurements, while biomechanical models describe how living tissue moves or deforms.
- **Medical robotics** connects those observations and models to assistance during an intervention, alongside interfaces designed around the clinician’s task.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Medical images] --> B[Models and planning]
 B --> C[Clinical guidance]
 C --> D[Evaluate assistance]
```

> **Key idea:** The target is a better-supported clinical action, not removing the clinician simply because a robot can move.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think coordinate conversion:** a location in an image and a physical tool position are different representations that must agree before an action makes sense.
- **Worked classroom example:** mark a target at pixel `(100, 80)`, then resize the image by half; its matching location becomes `(50, 40)`, not the original coordinates.
- **Study the software boundary:** image processing, modelling, and evaluation offer meaningful learning tasks without presenting a student prototype as a validated medical device.

## How to engage

1. **Read the GMCAO overview** to connect sensing, reasoning, and action to specific medical research questions.
2. **Watch TIMC’s researcher portrait** for context, then its continuum-robot modelling video for a more technical example.
3. **Use public team pages and scientific events** to identify relevant work; bring a reproducible nonclinical experiment and a narrowly defined question.

lessons.summary: Toyota Research Institute develops robotic capabilities and tools intended to amplify human abilities in realistic environments, including manufacturing.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Toyota Research Institute develops robotic capabilities and tools intended to amplify human abilities in realistic environments, including manufacturing.

![TRI mobile manipulation robot operating in a grocery-store setting](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-tri.webp)
*A TRI mobile-manipulation research robot in a grocery-store setting. Source: [Official source](https://www.tri.global/our-work/robotics), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mobile manipulation** combines movement through an environment with handling objects; TRI studies fleets of general-purpose prototype robots performing useful physical tasks.
- **Robot user experience** concerns how people interact with robots; TRI connects interface design to workers’ needs and manufacturing applications.
- **Research operations** include hardware prototyping and data collection, while technology-adoption work asks how research can leave the laboratory.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Task and user needs] --> B[Collect data]
 B --> C[Train and prototype]
 C --> D[Evaluate useful work]
```

> **Key idea:** A useful robot depends on the data, interface, and operating workflow around its learned behavior—not only the model itself.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a production ML service:** training code, data quality, monitoring, and user interaction all influence whether the system helps anyone.
- **Worked evaluation exercise:** for a pick-and-place demo, run ten trials and report both successful placements and human interventions; eight placements with six rescues tell a different story.
- **Study contact as well as vision:** TRI’s TACTIC paper uses tactile and visual information; tactile sensing measures contact instead of only looking at the scene.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official factory-training video** to understand the research setting before interpreting individual model results.
2. **Read the robotics programme page** and identify which pillar matches your team’s question: manipulation, interfaces, operations, or adoption.
3. **Follow public research publications** and reproduce a software-sized component; document your task and intervention rules rather than comparing highlight videos.

lessons.name: TU Berlin Robotics and Biology Laboratory (RBO)
lessons.summary: TU Berlin’s Robotics and Biology Laboratory studies adaptive robot behavior, including soft hands that exploit physical contact during manipulation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TU Berlin’s Robotics and Biology Laboratory studies adaptive robot behavior, including soft hands that exploit physical contact during manipulation.

![Soft robotic hand pictured in RBO’s manipulation research](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-rbo.webp)
*An RBO soft robotic hand, published in the lab’s manipulation research pages. Source: [Official source](https://www.tu.berlin/en/robotics/research-areas/soft-manipulation), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Soft manipulation** uses flexible robot bodies and fingers to handle objects; contact with the surroundings can help rather than always being avoided.
- **RBO Hand 3** is a pneumatic hand, meaning air pressure drives its actuators, the components that produce motion.
- **Interactive perception** uses action to learn about the world: moving or touching an object can reveal information a static camera image misses.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Soft hand design] --> B[Contact with object]
 B --> C[Observe grasp]
 C --> D[Adjust control]
```

> **Key idea:** Some of the intelligence in a grasp can come from the hand’s physical design instead of increasingly complicated control code.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think co-designing an API and runtime:** changing the underlying mechanism can simplify the software required to achieve the same task.
- **Worked observation exercise:** watch a grasp against a table edge; identify where the environment guides the object rather than treating every contact as an error.
- **Compare conditions:** note the object, wrist pose, and contact surface; apparent robustness is meaningful only relative to what actually changed between trials.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the lab’s manipulation study** before assuming that rigid, precisely modelled fingers are the only design option.
2. **Read the soft-manipulation explanation** to connect compliance, meaning mechanical flexibility, with control and sensing choices.
3. **Inspect the Hand 3 construction tutorial** before considering fabrication; start with reproducing an analysis or improving a documented step, not an unsupported hardware modification.

lessons.name: TU Darmstadt IAS (Intelligent Autonomous Systems)
lessons.summary: TU Darmstadt’s Intelligent Autonomous Systems group researches how robots can learn useful behavior rather than relying only on hand-written motion rules.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TU Darmstadt’s Intelligent Autonomous Systems group researches how robots can learn useful behavior rather than relying only on hand-written motion rules.

![Unitree G1 and Booster T1 humanoid robots listed on IAS’s robot page](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-ias.webp)
*Unitree G1 and Booster T1 listed by IAS; its page locates these robots at DFKI’s Systems AI for Robot Learning laboratory. Source: [Official source](https://www.ias.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de/Research/Robots), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Robot learning** develops behavior from data and experience; IAS investigates it across manipulation, human assistance, and mobile or legged platforms.
- **Reinforcement learning** improves decisions using feedback about outcomes; **imitation learning** instead starts from demonstrations of a task.
- **Research platforms** include humanoids, robots with human-like body arrangements, alongside robot arms and other systems; learning methods must respect each platform’s physical limits.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Task and observations] --> B[Learn a policy]
 B --> C[Test robot behavior]
 C --> D[Evaluate outcomes]
```

> **Key idea:** Learning an action policy does not remove the need to define the task, collect useful experience, and evaluate physical behavior.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think testing a learned function:** the input is an observation, the output is an action, and success requires more than a low training error.
- **Worked toy example:** reward a simulated agent for approaching an object, then check whether it stops there; distance alone does not specify “pick it up.”
- **Separate learning routes:** demonstrations, rewards, and hand-written rules encode different information, so record which ingredients your baseline actually uses.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the IAS research overview** to connect abstract learning methods to visible robot tasks.
2. **Read the research and robot pages** and choose one behavior rather than trying to reproduce every platform.
3. **Study a specific public demonstration** and its associated publication; report the observation, action, training signal, and evaluation conditions in a small reproducible experiment.

lessons.name: TU Dresden CeTI (Centre for Tactile Internet with Human-in-the-Loop)
lessons.summary: TU Dresden’s CeTI studies communication and human-machine interaction that let people and robots exchange skills across real and virtual environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TU Dresden’s CeTI studies communication and human-machine interaction that let people and robots exchange skills across real and virtual environments.

![Two modern robots face a historical drumming-bear automaton in CeTI’s museum film](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-ceti.webp)
*CeTI’s museum film contrasts modern robots with a historical automaton; image AVANGA Filmproduction. Source: [Official source](https://tu-dresden.de/tu-dresden/newsportal/news/Film-des-Exzellenzclusters-CeTI-Gewinner-des-Gold-Awards-der-US-International-Awards-2023-und-Platin-Auszeichnung-des-TITAN-Health-Awards), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Tactile Internet** concerns interaction that carries touch and action-related information, not just a video stream between distant places.
- **Human-in-the-loop** means the person remains part of the interacting system; CeTI combines engineering and computing with research on perception, action, and people.
- **Remote collaboration and telepresence** investigate working together across locations; telepresence means interacting with a distant environment through technology.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Human action] --> B[Network]
 B --> C[Remote robot]
 C --> D[Sensory feedback]
 D --> A
```

> **Key idea:** A remote robot interface must work for a person’s senses and actions, not merely deliver packets successfully.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think networked applications:** bandwidth is not the only concern; delay, timing, and feedback affect whether an interaction feels controllable.
- **Worked interface exercise:** compare a joystick display with immediate feedback and one delayed by half a second; log overshoot rather than only completed commands.
- **Keep claims separate:** a pleasant interface demonstration does not by itself establish reliable remote operation under all network conditions.

## How to engage

1. **Watch CeTI’s hackathon recap** to see one public-facing route into hands-on mobile robotics.
2. **Read the official cluster profile** for its human-centered research scope and current phase, rather than relying on a single application video.
3. **Explore public summer-school and outreach reports** and check new event eligibility individually; past participation formats are not a promise of future access.

lessons.name: TUM MIRMI (Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence)
lessons.summary: TUM MIRMI connects robotics and machine-intelligence research across disciplines to develop intelligent systems that interact with people and the physical world.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TUM MIRMI connects robotics and machine-intelligence research across disciplines to develop intelligent systems that interact with people and the physical world.

![MIRMI’s published photograph of the TUM RoboGym opening](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-mirmi.webp)
*Participants and robots at the TUM RoboGym opening, pictured on MIRMI’s website. Source: [Official source](https://www.mirmi.tum.de/en/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Machine intelligence** concerns systems that perceive, learn, and make decisions; MIRMI connects those methods to machines acting in physical environments.
- **Interdisciplinary research** links robot mechanisms, sensing, control, learning, and human interaction rather than treating each as a self-contained project.
- **Shared initiatives** connect university research with experimental infrastructure and practical applications; MIRMI’s public site also documents the TUM RoboGym opening.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Human needs] --> B[Hardware and software]
 B --> C[Physical experiments]
 C --> D[Evaluate system]
```

> **Key idea:** Better robot intelligence emerges from connecting algorithms, bodies, experiments, and human needs—not from choosing a model in isolation.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a systems architecture:** a team needs clear interfaces between camera data, learned decisions, control commands, and evaluation logs.
- **Worked planning exercise:** split a table-cleaning demo into perception, grasp choice, and movement; give each component one input, one output, and one failure condition.
- **Learn across specialties:** a software-focused team can use MIRMI’s breadth to identify missing mechanical or interaction assumptions without attempting to build every subsystem itself.

## How to engage

1. **Watch MIRMI’s introduction** to see the mix of people, machines, and application settings behind the institute’s name.
2. **Browse its research publication list** and select one paper before looking for supporting project material or code.
3. **Follow institute news and scientific events** and approach the relevant project’s public channel with a small reproducible result, not an undefined partnership request.

lessons.name: U2IS – ENSTA Paris
lessons.summary: ENSTA Paris’s U2IS research includes autonomous systems, robot navigation, perception, embedded vision, learning, and human-robot interaction.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ENSTA Paris’s U2IS research includes autonomous systems, robot navigation, perception, embedded vision, learning, and human-robot interaction.

![Mobile robots in an indoor navigation experiment shown by U2IS ENSTA Paris](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-u2is.webp)
*Published video thumbnail from the team’s interactive visual-navigation demonstration. Source: [U2IS ENSTA Paris](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9eFvc45H2ls), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Navigation** lets a mobile robot move toward a goal while using information about its surroundings; U2IS’s autonomous-systems team studies this with perception and learning.
- **Embedded vision** runs visual processing within a constrained robot system, rather than assuming unlimited offboard computing resources.
- **Depth estimation** predicts how far scene surfaces are from a camera; the team publishes code on rescaling such estimates using additional sensor information.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[Camera image] --> B[Estimate depth]
 B --> C[Rescale with sensor data]
 C --> D[Check metric distances]
```

> **Key idea:** A visually convincing scene estimate is not automatically a reliable measurement for deciding where a physical robot can move.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think typed data:** an array of depth-like values is not a usable distance interface until its scale and meaning are known.
- **Worked illustration:** if a depth estimate uses half the correct scale, an object actually two metres away appears one metre away; downstream decisions inherit that error.
- **Connect learning to the task:** a navigation demonstration can reveal what observations and interactions are needed, beyond a model’s standalone image benchmark.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the team’s navigation demonstration** and identify what the robot observes before deciding how to move.
2. **Read the autonomous-systems team description** to distinguish its research scope from ENSTA’s broader teaching programmes.
3. **Inspect the depth-rescaling implementation** and reproduce an existing example before proposing extensions; use public repository issues for specific reproducible software problems.

lessons.name: UK-RAS Network
lessons.summary: UK-RAS Network connects UK robotics and autonomous-systems research through community activities, public engagement, and shared research information.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

UK-RAS Network connects UK robotics and autonomous-systems research through community activities, public engagement, and shared research information.

![Event scene published on the UK-RAS Network website](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-ukras.webp)
*An experimental robot cell featured on the UK-RAS Network’s website. Source: [Official source](https://uk-ras.org.uk), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A research network** connects institutions and people; UK-RAS is not one laboratory building a single family of robots.
- **Public engagement** makes research visible through demonstrations and accessible conversations, including Robot Lab Live material distributed through Robot Talk.
- **Publications and showcases** provide routes into the community’s research topics and events without requiring beginners to understand every technical paper first.

> **Key idea:** A robotics network is useful for finding the right people and questions, not only for collecting organization names.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think an open-source community:** demonstrations, shared explanations, and research exchange can connect teams that do not share a campus or hardware stack.
- **Worked communication exercise:** turn one robot demo into a sixty-second explanation naming the task, sensor, action, and one visible limitation; avoid calling every subsystem “AI.”
- **Build relevant contacts:** use a specific research topic to identify a laboratory rather than sending the same broad sponsorship message to every network member.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a Robot Lab Live highlight** and write down one question that the short demonstration does not answer.
2. **Read the network introduction** and browse its publication catalogue to find topics related to your student project.
3. **Check official showcase announcements** for the actual format, audience, and registration conditions; an event listing does not guarantee that travel support or participation is available.

lessons.name: University of Basel BIROMED-Lab
lessons.summary: The University of Basel’s BIROMED-Lab develops robotic and mechatronic systems for medical training, diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The University of Basel’s BIROMED-Lab develops robotic and mechatronic systems for medical training, diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation.

![BIROMED-Lab research group pictured on its official university page](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-biromed.webp)
*The BIROMED-Lab group pictured on its official University of Basel page. Source: [Official source](https://dbe.unibas.ch/en/research/laser-and-robotics/bio-inspired-robots-for-medicine-lab/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mechatronics** combines mechanisms, electronics, and software; BIROMED develops medical systems from ideas into functioning prototypes.
- **Robot-assisted surgery** includes flexible endoscopes, instruments used to look inside the body, alongside force sensing and interfaces for controlling surgical tools.
- **Rehabilitation robotics** supports recovery and training; the FLOAT project studies robot-assisted walking and related movements, while SpineBot addresses spinal biomechanics.

> **Key idea:** Medical robotics includes training, measurement, assistance, and recovery—not only an autonomous machine performing surgery.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think several interfaces in one application:** the clinician, patient, sensors, and robot each impose different requirements on the same software system.
- **Worked software exercise:** replay a simulated force trace `[1, 2, 8]`; flag the last sample against a chosen classroom threshold of five, without claiming medical significance.
- **Treat validation seriously:** detecting a number in software is not proof that a sensor, robot, or treatment is safe or clinically useful.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the department’s Spinebot demonstration** to see one concrete device rather than imagining all medical robots as surgical arms.
2. **Browse the lab’s project descriptions** and choose a narrow question, such as sensing, control, or an interface design.
3. **Read the FLOAT research page** for a contrasting rehabilitation example; use published project contacts for focused nonclinical technical questions and keep student experiments off patients.

lessons.name: University of Bonn AIS (Autonomous Intelligent Systems)
lessons.summary: The University of Bonn’s Autonomous Intelligent Systems group develops robots that perceive and act in tasks including humanoid football and service robotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The University of Bonn’s Autonomous Intelligent Systems group develops robots that perceive and act in tasks including humanoid football and service robotics.

![Bonn’s NimbRo-OP2 humanoid robot at RoboCup 2017](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-bonn.webp)
*The earlier NimbRo-OP2 platform at RoboCup 2017; the linked video introduces the distinct OP2X platform. Source: [Official source](https://www.nimbro.net/OP/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Autonomous systems** use observations to choose and execute actions, rather than relying on a person to specify each movement.
- **NimbRo** is the group’s robotics project; its work includes humanoid football, service robots, and other perception-and-action problems.
- **NimbRo-OP2X** is an open-source adult-sized humanoid platform; its published material connects physical construction with walking, perception, and robot behavior.

> **Key idea:** A football robot needs perception, decisions, and movement to succeed together under changing conditions—not merely a good ball detector.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think an integration benchmark:** a match repeatedly exposes timing and coordination failures that separate unit tests can miss.
- **Worked exercise:** label a recorded ball as left, center, or right; map those three labels to turn-left, approach, or turn-right commands in a toy simulation.
- **Keep the distinction clear:** this simple policy illustrates one decision interface; it does not solve balance, collision avoidance, or full football behavior.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the OP2X platform introduction** and separate what the hardware enables from what the software must still learn or control.
2. **Read the humanoid and platform pages** for the project’s actual research context before considering a hardware build.
3. **Browse the group’s research overview** and follow project-specific publications or open releases; share a small reproducible perception or simulation result rather than assuming competition participation is trivial.

lessons.name: University of Geneva MIRALab
lessons.summary: MIRALab is a University of Geneva–linked research lab that builds digital humans, extended reality and social robots such as Nadine.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MIRALab is a University of Geneva–linked research lab that builds digital humans, extended reality and social robots such as Nadine.

![MIRALab composite image of a realistic virtual human face](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-miralab.webp)
*A digital-human composite from MIRALab. Source: [MIRALab](https://miralab.ch/about-miralab/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Digital humans** are computer-made people that look, move and react like real ones, in games, XR or research.
- **Extended reality (XR)** covers virtual and augmented reality, where people and virtual characters share one scene.
- **Social robotics** puts that human-like behaviour into a physical body; the lab’s best-known example is the map node Nadine social robot.

> **Key idea:** A social robot is mostly a software problem: perception, dialogue and believable reactions matter as much as motors.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software-first entry point:** think of Nadine as a chatbot with a face, ears and a body, where every output must be timed with gestures.
- **Interaction exercise:** script a ten-line dialogue and mark where a robot should nod, look, or pause; that timing table is a real HRI design artefact.
- **Watch out:** a lifelike face can make people over-trust a system, so state clearly what your robot cannot understand.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Nadine museum video** and note which reactions look natural and which feel delayed.
2. **Read the About MIRALab page** to see how graphics, XR and robotics connect in one lab.
3. **Browse the Nadine site** for the robot’s official description before citing any claim about it.

lessons.name: University of Hamburg TAMS (Technical Aspects of Multimodal Systems)
lessons.summary: TAMS is a University of Hamburg computer-science group studying how robots combine several senses to manipulate objects, learn skills and work with people.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TAMS is a University of Hamburg computer-science group studying how robots combine several senses to manipulate objects, learn skills and work with people.

![The two HOAP-2 humanoid robots of the TAMS group](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-tams.webp)
*Two HOAP-2 humanoid robots used by TAMS. Source: [TAMS Robotics](https://tams.informatik.uni-hamburg.de/research/robotics/index.php), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Multimodal** means using more than one sense, such as vision, touch and force, in the same control loop.
- **Sensor-based manipulation** is grasping and moving objects while reacting to what the sensors report, not following a blind script.
- **Robot learning and human–robot interaction (HRI)** are further research areas; master students demonstrate projects like bi-manual Rubik’s Cube solving.
- **Hamburg Bit-Bots** is the university’s RoboCup humanoid-soccer workgroup; its software uses ROS 2, Python and C++ on GitHub.

> **Key idea:** Fusing senses is like merging several unreliable APIs: each one is noisy, but together they give a trustworthy state.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Familiar stack:** Bit-Bots code is ROS 2 packages in Python and C++, so reading it feels like reading a large open-source backend.
- **Fusion exercise:** log a camera estimate and a fake touch signal for one grasp; write a rule that trusts touch once contact happens.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Rubik’s Cube master-project demo** and list which senses each step needs.
2. **Watch the Bit-Bots application video** to see a full humanoid-soccer software stack in action.
3. **Read the TAMS research overview** for the group’s own list of topics.
4. **Explore the Bit-Bots GitHub organisation** and open one ROS 2 package to trace its inputs and outputs.

lessons.summary: The University of Zurich Robotics and Perception Group builds drones that navigate autonomously using only onboard cameras and computers.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The University of Zurich Robotics and Perception Group builds drones that navigate autonomously using only onboard cameras and computers.

![First-person view from a racing drone flying toward red racing gates](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-rpg.webp)
*A drone’s-eye view of a racing track used in RPG drone-racing research. Source: [UZH RPG](https://rpg.ifi.uzh.ch/research.html), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Onboard autonomy** means the drone senses and decides with its own cameras and computer, without external motion-capture help.
- **Drone racing** is a stress test: the group notes it combines dynamics modelling, perception, localization, trajectory planning and control.
- **Deep reinforcement learning (RL)** trains a policy by trial and error in simulation; the group reported champion-level racing this way in Nature (2023).
- **Flightmare** is the group’s open quadrotor simulator with Unity rendering, physics, multiple sensors and parallel environments for RL.

> **Key idea:** Fast flight leaves no time for slow code: perception and control must run inside a tight real-time loop.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Simulation first:** Flightmare lets students train and break policies without crashing real hardware.
- **Latency exercise:** in any simple drone simulator, add a 50 ms delay to sensor readings and watch how a controller’s tracking error changes.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the champion-level drone racing video** and note what the drone sees versus what it does.
2. **Read the research page** to see the group’s main topics beyond racing.
3. **Clone Flightmare** and run one example environment.
4. **Browse the software and datasets page** for released code and data to reproduce.

lessons.summary: Wyss Zurich is a University of Zurich and ETH Zurich centre that helps research teams turn robotics and medical technology into real products and start-ups.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Wyss Zurich is a University of Zurich and ETH Zurich centre that helps research teams turn robotics and medical technology into real products and start-ups.

![Tethys Robotics underwater drone](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-wyss.webp)
*Tethys Robotics’ underwater drone, a Wyss Zurich robotics project. Source: [Wyss Zurich](https://www.wysszurich.ch/projects/tethys-robotics-ag/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Translational research** means pushing a lab result toward a usable product; Wyss Zurich hosts teams during that step.
- **ANYbotics** developed the ANYmal legged inspection robot there under the project name ANYmotion (2016–2019).
- **Wingtra** built a mapping drone that takes off vertically like a helicopter and flies like an airplane.
- **Voliro and Tethys** work on flying robots that touch structures and an underwater drone for turbid, rough waters.

> **Key idea:** A demo that works in a lab is not a product; the hard part is making it reliable for real customers.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Start-up path:** the project pages show how academic robots became companies, which matches a startup-style lab.
- **Product exercise:** pick one project page and write a one-page spec: user, task, environment and failure that would end a pilot.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the ANYmotion video** to see a lab robot framed as an industrial product.
2. **Watch the 11-year highlights video** for the range of projects.
3. **Browse the robotics project list** and read two project pages end to end.
4. **Read the Tethys project page** as a concrete example of a robot built for a harsh environment.

lessons.name: ZHAW Institute of Mechatronic Systems (IMS)
lessons.summary: ZHAW’s Institute of Mechatronic Systems is a Swiss applied-research institute that develops robotics and mechatronic systems with industry and teaches systems engineering.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ZHAW’s Institute of Mechatronic Systems is a Swiss applied-research institute that develops robotics and mechatronic systems with industry and teaches systems engineering.

![A person working next to a robot arm in ZHAW’s MINDLab](/img/lessons/orgs_research_lab_4-ims.webp)
*Human–robot collaboration work in the IMS MINDLab. Source: [ZHAW MINDLab](https://www.zhaw.ch/en/engineering/institutes-centres/ims/mindlab), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mechatronics** combines mechanics, electronics and software in one machine; IMS has around 60 employees across six R&D focus areas.
- **Human–robot collaboration (HRC)** is when people and robots share a workspace; MINDLab studies it directly.
- **MINDLab topics** include environment monitoring, contact detection, human action recognition and predictive collision avoidance.

> **Key idea:** Safe collaboration is a perception problem: the robot must notice people before it touches them.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **AI fit:** action recognition and collision prediction are vision and ML problems that software students can prototype first.
- **Detection exercise:** run a pose-estimation model on a short webcam clip and flag frames where a hand enters a marked “robot zone”.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the contact-detection video** embedded on the MINDLab page.
2. **Watch the institute introduction video** for an overview of IMS.
3. **Read the MINDLab page** to see the lab’s research list and equipment.
4. **Read the IMS overview** for its focus areas and teaching role.
